# Wiring Audit - Dead-Function Scan

**Base commit:** `2bf9a46d` (merge of #438), triaged on top of the #437 scan.
**Generated by:** `python scripts/check_wiring.py --json`. The tables below are
produced from an actual run, not maintained by hand, so they cannot drift from
what the gate actually reports.

**Gate impact:** none. The scan stays `--method-findings=warn`. Only ERROR
findings fail the gate, and the blocking pass output is byte-identical to #437.

## Outcome

| | count |
|---|---|
| Findings reported by #437 | 32 |
| Detector false positives, fixed | 4 findings |
| Genuinely dead declarations removed | 22 |
| Remaining, genuinely unwired | 5 |

The backlog is not zero, and it should not be. The remaining 5 are
**unwired features** -- not dead code, and not detector noise. Each has a KDoc
stating an intended caller that does not exist. They stay flagged, because they
are real defects of a different kind.

## Remaining findings - UNWIRED, not dead

| Symbol | Location | Why it is not dead code |
|---|---|---|
| `GhostIdentityGate.shouldRenderAsNode` | `data/GhostIdentityGate.kt:63` | Documented as a UI convenience ("never let a ghost be online") but no UI calls it. GhostIdentityGateTest calls it directly, so the code is exercised while the app never reaches it -- the decideCommand shape: tests green, feature absent. |
| `TransportManager.attemptEscalation` | `transport/TransportManager.kt:327` | KDoc says "Called when a peer is discovered on BLE". No such call site exists, so BLE-to-WiFi escalation never runs. The implementation is intact and self-contained. |
| `BleScanner.onTransportPause` | `transport/ble/BleScanner.kt:606` | KDoc says "Called when the app is backgrounded or the user explicitly pauses BLE". No call site exists. BleScannerTest covers it directly, so BLE pause-on-background is unwired. |
| `ChatViewModel.getRetryDelayForAttempt` | `ui/viewmodels/ChatViewModel.kt:390` | KDoc says "for display in message retry timing". No UI reads it. |
| `MainViewModel.consumeRequestsInboxNav` | `ui/viewmodels/MainViewModel.kt:413` | Sibling consumeChatNav() IS called from the UI. The requests-inbox equivalent has no caller, so that navigation target is never consumed. |

Deleting these would discard working implementations of intended behaviour.
Wiring them is new behaviour and out of scope for a triage pass. Each needs a
product decision: wire it, or delete it along with its test.

## Detector bugs found and fixed

All four were false positives caused by the detector modelling Kotlin wrongly.
Each is pinned by a self-test case in `scripts/test_check_wiring.py`.

| False positive | Reality | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| `MeshSyncWorkerEntryPoint.getMeshRepository` | Hilt @EntryPoint accessor called by MeshSyncWorker.doWork | see root causes below |
| `MeshRepository.getMeshService` | called by MeshSyncWorker.doWork | see root causes below |
| `AnrWatchdog.isMainThreadResponsive` | called at AnrWatchdog.kt:207 in the diagnostics string | see root causes below |
| `SmartTransportRouter.getPreferredTransport` | called at SmartTransportRouter.kt:370 inside attemptDelivery | see root causes below |

Three root causes:

1. **`override` and `private` functions were invisible as scopes.** They are
   deliberately not reachability targets so they are not collected -- but the
   reference map also used them to decide which scope a line sits in. A call
   inside an `override` body was attributed to the nearest preceding tracked
   declaration and then discarded as a self-reference.
   Fix: `collect_scope_ranges` records brace-depth ranges for every class AND
   function, including the untracked ones.

2. **Line proximity cannot model nesting.** `SmartTransportRouter` declares
   `data class TransportAttempt` *inside* the function `attemptDelivery`, so
   "nearest preceding declaration" picked the inner class for lines that the
   function actually contains. Fix: a line is attributed to the smallest range
   that contains it.

3. **A class whose opening brace is on a later line was dropped.**
   `class MeshRepository @Inject constructor(` has no opening brace on its own
   line, so the class never entered the scope stack and every fqcn inside it
   lost the class name. That turned live self-calls into apparent external
   callers and marked nine LIVE methods dead. This was caught by re-checking
   every resolution against the source. Fix: the declaration is deferred and
   pushed when its brace appears, matching the original extractor's
   `pending_class` handling.

Self-detection also had to stop comparing names alone. An anonymous
`object : Callback { override fun onStartSuccess() }` computes the same
qualified name as the outer method it delegates to, so `this@Outer.m()` would
look recursive. The scope's start line is compared instead.

## Checks performed before classifying anything

- `src/test` and `src/androidTest` are outside the reference corpus, so no test
  caller can make a function look wired to production.
- Zero `.java` sources under `android/`, so there is no Java caller the scan misses.
- No reflective string invocation of any flagged symbol.
- No flagged symbol is an `override`, an implemented interface member, an
  `@EntryPoint` accessor, or a serialization hook -- so none of them qualifies
  for a detector exemption. Every exemption route was therefore available and
  none was needed.
- The detector scans `android/app/src/main` (105 of 180 Kotlin files).
  `android/shared/` and `shared/` are outside the corpus. Checked explicitly:
  none of the 32 findings was referenced from those roots, so the gap caused
  none of them. Recorded as a known limitation rather than silently ignored.

## Promotion

Still `--method-findings=warn`, deliberately. The remaining findings need
product decisions, not a policy change: each is either a feature that should be
wired or code that should go. Once those are resolved, promoting is a one-word
change.
